coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Lateral row only. Frames cropped from the full scan at 0.9x with 25 px grids labelled in scan pixels (contrast 1.15). Joint points (shoulder, wrist, hip = greater trochanter, knee, ankle, toe) read off the grid, drawn back as dots and lines (pl152/sheet-v*.png in the scratch folder) and checked. Frames 2-3: 'knee/ankle/toe' is the take-off leg, '*Lead' the leg swung up first; frame 4: the trailing leg; frames 9-12: the visible (landing) leg. In frames 5-8 the legs fold over each other at the bar, so only the hip, shoulder and lowest toe are recorded there. Ground line: about y 1767 in frames 1-3, about 1755 in frames 5-8, about 1744 in frames 11-12 (the floor is seen at a slight angle). Angle conventions as in human-pl162.json. Leg length about 195 px. The figure is small, so point accuracy is about +-6 px (3% of leg length) but angles are only good to about +-8 deg.
derivedKey: derived: leg (px), knee (deg, interior), thigh/shin (deg from straight down, + forward), trunkLean (deg from vertical, + forward), arm (deg from straight down, + forward), ankleAngle (deg, interior knee-ankle-toe); *Lead for the lead leg

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a cycle shown on the plate)
timing.computed: 11 intervals x 87 ms between frame 1 and frame 12 (the whole jump from the last approach stride to landing)

frames.notes: Last approach stride: support leg bent (knee 119 deg), other foot behind in the air. Hip 173 px above the ground = 0.89 leg lengths.
Take-off: support leg straight (178 deg) on the toes, lead thigh kicked up to horizontal (87 deg), lead knee 128 deg; trunk upright, fists forward at shoulder height.
Airborne: take-off foot 50 px off the ground, lead thigh above horizontal (109 deg).
Both legs drawn up: trailing knee 77 deg, lead leg reaching over the bar; arms forward.
Full tuck over the bar: both knees folded, thighs pulled to the chest (knee angles not separable), trunk 20 deg forward.
Tucked, the lead foot reaching forward past the bar.
Highest hip in the sequence (y 1417, 338 px above the ground). Legs unfolding downward.
Legs extending down; arms coming up.
Descending, trunk leaning back 13 deg, one arm thrown up overhead (135 deg), knees 120 deg.
Legs reaching down for the ground (knee 148 deg), trunk leaning back 19 deg, arm up 150 deg.
Toes about 16 px above the ground: touch-down is imminent (between frames 11 and 12).
Landed, absorbing: knee 107 deg, hip 161 px above the ground = 0.83 leg lengths (drop 0.17), trunk upright.

findings: Timing (87 ms intervals): take-off foot leaves the ground between frames 2 and 3 and the feet land between frames 11 and 12, so air time is about 9 intervals = 0.78 s (range 0.70-0.87 s); the hip peaks at frame 7 (t 0.52 s), a little after mid-flight. Ground phases in the plate are only one approach frame and one landing frame, so preparation and recovery are not covered.

Our human.jump (1.0 s, air 0.42 = 0.42 s): this running high jump stays in the air almost twice as long (0.78 s). For a game jump over a high obstacle, an air fraction nearer 0.6-0.7 of a 1.0-1.2 s action would match it.

Take-off is a single-leg drive with no deep crouch: the last approach stride has the hip at 0.89 leg lengths (knee 119 deg), and at take-off the support leg is straight (178 deg) while the lead thigh swings up to horizontal. Our dip 8 (0.22 leg lengths, two-footed crouch) does not apply to a running jump.

Tuck: trailing knee 77 deg in frame 4, then both thighs pulled to the chest over the bar (frames 5-6); the lowest toe rises to about 240 px (1.2 leg lengths) above the ground while the hip rises about 127 px (0.65 leg lengths) above its take-off height. Our tuck 8 (0.22 leg lengths) is far smaller.

Lean and arms: trunk upright at take-off (-3 to 0 deg), 19-20 deg forward over the bar, then 9-19 deg BACK on the way down as the legs reach for the ground; one arm swings up overhead (135-161 deg) for balance during the descent. Our lean 8 forward then back (rot lean x (1 - 1.6k)) has the same forward-then-back shape.
Landing: hip drop 0.17 leg lengths, knee 107 deg in frame 12 (deeper absorption may follow after the plate ends).

Not measured: knee angles in frames 5-8 (legs folded over each other), elbows, the bar height (the bar itself could not be told from the background lines with confidence), jump distance (separate cameras), the front row.
